note: Researched recommendations, written in the site's voice but by somebody who has not been. Opinionated on purpose — a list of facts is not a guide — but every card says plainly that it was researched rather than visited, and a handwritten note in notes.json overrules any of it.
rules: Every record needs a source and a lastVerified date. If it cannot be checked, it does not go in.
Say what to order and when to go. 'Lovely atmosphere' helps nobody.
Set touristy: true for anywhere that is a sight rather than a local habit — it stays eligible for Culture and Worth the trip, and drops out of the everyday sections.
quality and uniqueness cap at 4 here. 5 is reserved for somewhere one of you actually loved.

items.title: Coutume
items.why: One of the roasters that started Paris taking coffee seriously, and still roasting. The rue de Babylone room is bright and full of people working, which makes it better for a long morning than a quick stop.
items.source: Published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Terres de Café
items.why: A roaster first and a counter second — come for beans to take home as much as for the cup. Useful in a quarter where the alternative is a hotel lobby.

items.title: Café Joyeux
items.why: A social-enterprise café staffed by people with intellectual disabilities and autism, on the Champs-Élysées of all places. The coffee is good; the reason to go is that it exists and works.

items.title: Siempre
items.why: Specialty coffee in a quarter that has very little of it. Small, and the sort of place that knows where its beans came from.

items.title: Bel Horizon Cofee Roaster
items.why: Roasting on site in Vaugirard. Worth the walk if you have been making do with the café on the corner.

items.title: Moncœur Belleville

items.title: Sébastien Gaudard
items.why: Classical French pâtisserie made properly, with none of the modern gimmickry. The tarts are the thing.

items.title: Aki Boulangerie
items.why: Japanese-French baking near the Opéra — matcha, azuki and yuzu worked into French pastry rather than bolted on.

items.title: Stohrer
items.why: Opened in 1730 by Louis XV's pastry chef, which makes it the oldest pâtisserie in Paris. The baba au rhum was invented here. The interior is listed.

items.title: The French Bastards
items.why: Modern, loud and very good at the sweet end. Expect a queue at the weekend and go on a Tuesday instead.

items.title: Arnaud Delmontel
items.why: A Grand Prix de la Baguette winner, and the baguette is still why you go. The pastry counter is a bonus.

items.title: Pâtisserie des Martyrs
items.why: Gaudard's shop on the rue des Martyrs, which is itself one of the better food streets in Paris. Do the street as well as the shop.

items.title: Vandermeersch
items.why: Out by Porte Dorée and worth the journey for the kouglof, which they have been making the same way for decades. Weekends only for some of it — check before you go.

items.title: Desgranges

items.title: Maison Landemaine

items.title: Benoit Castel

items.title: Les Zygomates
items.why: A former butcher's shop with the marble and mirrors left in, doing straightforward bistro cooking at a fair price. Book at the weekend.

items.title: Le Temps des cerises
